text.p: THURSDAY, JUNE 26

LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU foreign ministers meet (0930/0730 GMT). Agenda includes follow-up to Amsterdam EU summit; relations with Switzerland; outcome of G7 meeting; outcome of EU-Canada summit; outcome of EU-Japan summit; relations with Australia; mid-term revision of decision on association with overseas territories; situation in Albania, Burma, former Yugoslavia; Middle East peace process; extension of Great Lakes Regions envoy's mandate - followed by European Economic Area ministerial meeting.

LUXEMBOURG - EU education ministers meet (1000/0800 GMT). Agenda includes public hearing on "Education, training, research: barriers to trans-national mobility" (1030/0830 GMT); safety in school; information technologies; SOCRATES student exchange programme; "Teaching and learning: towards a cognitive society"; learning foreign languages; quality in higher education. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission regular weekly meeting (1500/1300 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Commissioners Monti and Bonino on financial services - strengthening consumer confidence.
- Commissioner Van Miert proposed decision under the merger regulation.
- Commissioners Marin and Brittan document on perspectives and priorities for the Asia-Europe Meeting process.
- Commissioner van den Broek on an interim accord with Armenia and Georgia.

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds mini session (0900/0700 GMT) (second of two days). Agenda includes: Council of Ministers and European Commission statements on the outcome of the Amsterdam EU summit; Dutch statement on their EU presidency.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana presents metal to General Georges Joulwan, Supreme Allied Commander Europe, on the occasion of his farewell ceremony (1245/1045 GMT).

BRUSSELS - The American European Community Association (AECA) holds round table on "Electronic commerce and trans-Atlantic relations" (1900/1700 GMT). Venue: to be confirmed. Contact: AECA (322) 344 5949.
LONDON - Congress on "Digital television - Economics, regulation and strategy" (To June 27). Venue: Le Meridien. Contact: Fiona Walker (44) 171 421 3500.
NORROEPING, Sweden - EU Committee of the Regions holds seminar on "Transport problems in the Baltic area". Contact: Committee of the Regions (322) 282 2155.
FRIDAY, JUNE 27
AMSTERDAM (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU will brief central and eastern European countries on the outcome of the EU Amsterdam summit. Participants include European Commissioner Van den Broek.

LUXEMBOURG - EU telecommunications ministers meet (1000/0800 GMT). They will adopt texts on satellite communications, telephone numbering policy and implementation by EU states of telecoms liberalisation rules. The European Commission will present reports on the new generation of mobile communications, EU participation in World Radiocommunications Conferences and illegal and harmful content on the Internet.

LUXEMBOURG - EU social affairs ministers meet (1500/1300 GMT). Agenda includes burden of proof in sex discrimination cases; workers' protection against cancer agents at work; interim report on employment; modernising and improving social protection; European systems of worker involvement in company decisions; worker consultation; "social dialogue" between management and labour groups.
COPENHAGEN - The Danish High Court rules on a challenge to the legality of Denmark's European Union treaties.
BRUSSELS - Forum Europe holds n/conf to launch the U.N. children/AIDS programme (1100/0900 GMT). Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: Forum Europe (322) 736 1430.
SATURDAY, JUNE 28
No events scheduled.
SUNDAY, JUNE 29
No events scheduled.
